title_en: Cheque Bounce: Section 138 NI Act Legal Notice, Deadlines & Court Complaint
title_hi: चेक बाउंस: धारा 138 एनआई एक्ट कानूनी नोटिस, समय-सीमा और अदालत में परिवाद

laws.plain_meaning: Where a cheque drawn for discharge of any debt or other liability is returned by the bank unpaid (due to insufficient funds or exceeding arrangement), it is a criminal offence punishable with imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine up to twice the cheque amount, or both.

Cognizance of offence: strict procedural timelines must be met. (a) Cheque presented within validity (3 months); (b) Legal demand notice sent within 30 days of receiving return memo; (c) Drawer gets 15 days to pay from receipt; (d) If unpaid, complaint must be filed in court within 1 month from the expiry of the 15-day period.

Offences by companies: if the person committing offence under s.138 is a company/firm, every person in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business, as well as the company itself, shall be deemed guilty.
Trial court may order the drawer of the cheque to pay interim compensation to the complainant not exceeding 20% of the cheque amount during trial.

steps.action_en: Present the cheque to the bank within its validity period (3 months from the date written on the cheque). Obtain the official Cheque Return Memo showing reason for dishonour (e.g. 'Funds Insufficient', 'Account Closed', 'Stop Payment').
steps.action_hi: चेक जारी होने की तारीख से 3 महीने के भीतर बैंक में प्रस्तुत करें। बैंक से अनादरण की आधिकारिक पर्ची (रिटर्न मेमो) प्राप्त करें।
steps.deadline_or_limitation: Within 3 months from date of cheque

steps.action_en: Send a formal Demand Notice in writing to the drawer demanding payment of the cheque amount, dispatched by Registered Post with Acknowledgment Due (RPAD) or Speed Post within 30 days of receiving the bank memo.
steps.action_hi: बैंक रिटर्न मेमो मिलने के 30 दिनों के भीतर देनदार को रजिस्टर्ड डाक / स्पीड पोस्ट से 15 दिनों का कानूनी नोटिस भेजें।
steps.where: Dispatched via India Post (Registered Post AD / Speed Post) to debtor's verified address
steps.deadline_or_limitation: Strictly within 30 calendar days from the date of receiving return memo from bank
documents_needed: Copy of Statutory Legal Demand Notice
India Post tracking consignment delivery report / signed AD card

steps.action_en: Wait 15 days from the date the drawer receives the notice (or deemed service). The law gives the drawer 15 clear days to make payment.
steps.action_hi: नोटिस प्राप्त होने की तारीख से 15 दिन तक भुगतान की प्रतीक्षा करें। कानून देनदार को भुगतान के लिए 15 दिन देता है।
steps.deadline_or_limitation: 15 days from date of delivery of notice
documents_needed: Delivery confirmation report from India Post website

steps.action_en: If no payment is received within the 15-day window, file a formal Criminal Complaint under Section 138 read with Section 142 of the NI Act before the Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate within 30 days (1 month) of the cause of action arising.
steps.action_hi: 15 दिन पूरे होने के बाद भी भुगतान न होने पर, अगले 1 महीने (30 दिन) के भीतर सक्षम मजिस्ट्रेट अदालत में धारा 138 के तहत परिवाद पेश करें।
steps.where: Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) / Metropolitan Magistrate (where payee bank branch is situated under s.142(2))
steps.deadline_or_limitation: Within 1 month (30 days) from the 16th day after notice delivery
documents_needed: Formal Complaint petition under s.138 NI Act with verification affidavit
Office copy of the Statutory Legal Notice
Original Postal Receipts and Delivery Tracking Report
Proof of underlying legally enforceable debt (invoice, agreement, ledger statement, promissory note)

steps.action_en: File an application under Section 143A NI Act along with or post-cognizance seeking 20% interim compensation from the accused.
steps.action_hi: अदालत में धारा 143A के तहत आवेदन देकर कुल चेक राशि का 20% अंतरिम मुआवजा दिलाने का अनुरोध करें।
steps.deadline_or_limitation: At the stage of framing of notice/charge or plea of not guilty

helplines.name: NALSA Legal Aid Helpline
helplines.description: Assistance for citizens eligible for free legal counsel to draft notice and file complaint

free_legal_aid.eligible: Any individual whose annual income is within the state ceiling (generally Rs. 3,00,000 in most states), women, senior citizens, and disadvantaged groups under Section 12 of Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
free_legal_aid.how_to_apply: Apply at the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) at the local court complex. A legal aid lawyer will be assigned to draft the statutory notice and conduct the trial.

when_to_see_a_lawyer: Immediately upon receiving the cheque bounce memo — the 30-day statutory notice clock starts ticking right away
When calculating jurisdictional bank branch under Section 142(2) NI Act to avoid filing in wrong court
If drawer is a company, to correctly implead active directors under Section 141 NI Act
